body: Reason(s) for non-compliance: • The Lead Agency does not pay all provider types prospectively or alternatively does not demonstrate that it is not a generally-accepted practice for all provider types, as required by 98.45(m)(1). (Plan Question 4.4.1a). Please note the Lead Agency has an approved waiver for this requirement through August 1, 2026. Overall Target Completion Date: 03/30/2026 Action Step Number Action Step Description Target Completion Date 1 July 1, 2024, Connecticut Public Act No. 24-91 repealed the regulations that governed the Care 4 Kids child care subsidy program. P.A. No. 24-91 further directed the Commissioner of the OEC to implement the provisions of 45 CFR 98 in order to administer the child care program and to develop policies and procedures necessary to implement such program. 09/30/2024 Create a framework for policy manual that aligns with Federal Rules. 2 Apply for ASSIST Technical Assistant support from the National Center for Subsidy Innovation and Accountability to develop and implement C4K policy manual. 10/16/2024 3 Hold three state-wide listening session with parent and providers to identify changes to C4K program. Use feedback to inform policy manual changes. 01/02/2025 4 OEC Policy team with support of ASSIST TA staff will draft C4K Policy Manual. OEC Policy team consults with OEC Leadership for feedback and edits OEC Policy team works with C4K team on the development of business processes related to revised policy. OEC consults with Deloitte IT team for policy changes that would require IT system updates. 10/30/2025 5 Begin phased-in rollout of C4K policy changes including paying provider prospectively. Update IT system based on policy changes. Develop and implement a communication plan with support from communication contractor at OEC. Pay all providers prospectively. 03/30/2026

body: Reason(s) for non-compliance: • The Lead Agency does not provide grants or contracts for direct services for infants and toddlers, for children in underserved geographic areas, and for children with disabilities, as required by 98.30(b)(1). (Plan Questions 4.1.1c and 4.5.1i). Please note the Lead Agency has an approved waiver for this requirement through August 1, 2026. Overall Target Completion Date: 01/01/2026 Action Step Number Action Step Description Target Completion Date 1 CCDF Team will work with Social Finance business consultants and OEC’s Early Care and Education team to develop a 3-5 year CCDF strategic plan which will include all new federal rule changes including development of a contracting pilot for direct services for an identified populations in the federal rule. The pilot will support the OEC’s vision to integrate all state and 05/30/2025 federal funding streams to create one point of entry for families. 2 CCDF team will work with Deloitte, IT consultants, to complete any system changes to support contracting pilot. 06/30/2025 3 Select eligible child care providers to participate in contracting pilot. 08/30/2025 4 Train selected provider on CCDF rules and contract requirements. 10/30/2025 5 Contracts executed. 01/30/2026

body: Reason(s) for non-compliance: • The Lead Agency does not adequately describe strategies to improve the supply and quality of child care during non-traditional hours, as required by 98.16(y) and (aa). (Plan Question 4.5.4d) Overall Target Completion Date: 07/30/2025 Action Step Number Action Step Description Target Completion Date 1 The OEC, Data Scientist will draft a child care needs assessment study. The study will include data and analysis of the supply and demand of nontraditional hours of care providers. 03/30/2025 2 The data from the study will be used to identify strategies to increase the supply of nontraditional hour care. 04/30/2025 3 The CCDF Policy team will work with other OEC team leads in other divisions who oversee projects related to child care supply building. Three promising projects in development: 05/30/2025 Tri-Share Child Care ￿ Program establish through Connecticut’s House Bill 5002. Pilot will focus on large employer in the New London area. The program is employer, state and employee fund matching program to lower the child care cost for employees. An additional program focus will include increasing the child care supply for 2nd shift workers. First Responder Referral Process - The enhanced referral service for first responders includes referrals to childcare programs that have been prescreened by 211 Child Care Referral Specialists for availability and the specific needs of families. First responders using this service received detailed program profiles, which include licensing inspection reports, hours, fees, capacity, meals, and special needs experience information for each prescreened program, a parent resource packet, connection to all 211 resources, and a follow-up call to check on outcomes and offer further referrals if needed. Team is tracking the requests for nontraditional hours. Data will be used to help build supply. Staffed Family Child Care Networks ￿ OEC will work closely with SFCCN Hub contractor to support providers interested in expanding business to serve families seeking nontraditional hour of care. 4 Implement supply building strategy for increasing the supply of nontraditional hours of care. 07/30/2025
